stem:
Qasim has the sorted scores $5$, $7$, $9$, $11$, $13$ (median $9$). He inserts the value $15$ into the list.

Which two claims correctly describe how the median changes?

One or more options may be correct.

options.text: After inserting $15$, the sorted list is $5$, $7$, $9$, $11$, $13$, $15$; the middle pair is $9$ and $11$, so the median becomes $10$.
Say the median moves after inserting $15$, skipping that the list must stay sorted and the new middle position(s) must be checked.
The median moves upward because $15$ is greater than the earlier median $9$.
Use the same middle-tracking rule to decide how the mean changes when $15$ is inserted.

teacher.key_rationale: Inserting $15$ above the old median yields sorted $5,7,9,11,13,15$; the middle pair averages to $10$, so the median rises. Skipping the sorted middle check, or stretching the rule to the mean, miss that hinge.
